title: BUG: Fix bandstructure legend for figures with multiple axes
body:
Fixes issue whereby `Bandstructure.plot(...)` would not plot the legend in cases where `self.ax` belongs to a figure with multiple axes by explicitly calling `self.ax.legend(...)` instead of `plt.legend(...)`.

Also fixes a minor bug in an error message in `band_structure.py`.

comments.body:
Thank you @elinscott for the fix!

I could reproduce the issue with the following script, which is fixed in the present MR.
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from ase.build import bulk
from ase.calculators.test import FreeElectrons

a = bulk('Cu')
a.calc = FreeElectrons(nvalence=1, kpts={'path': 'GXWLGK', 'npoints': 200})
a.get_potential_energy()
bs = a.calc.band_structure()
fig0, ax0 = plt.subplots()
fig1, ax1 = plt.subplots()  # make another set of (fig, ax) plt refers
bs.plot(ax=ax0, emin=0, emax=20, label="Cu")  # We should have a legend on ax0.
fig0.savefig("cu.png")
```
I also found a similar issue for `filename`, so, taking this opportunity, I also added the fix for it. That issue is checked with:
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from ase.build import bulk
from ase.calculators.test import FreeElectrons

a = bulk('Cu')
a.calc = FreeElectrons(nvalence=1, kpts={'path': 'GXWLGK', 'npoints': 200})
a.get_potential_energy()
bs = a.calc.band_structure()
fig0, ax0 = plt.subplots()
fig1, ax1 = plt.subplots()  # make another set of (fig, ax) plt refers
bs.plot(ax=ax0, emin=0, emax=20, label="Cu", filename="cu.png")
```
For normal cases we should add tests for these, but since testing of figure plotting is a bit tricky (although not impossible), I am going to merge.
